title: Ulyana and the Vow
premise: Beatrix Blackwood has built her career on erasure—ghostwriting the glittering memoir of rival author Camille Voss while hiding behind a vow she made eleven years ago to never be seen. When a lost letter surfaces, postmarked a decade past and addressed to Julian Ashford, the man whose heart she broke by vanishing, Beatrix realizes her invisibility was never protection but cowardice. As ghostwriting Camille's memoir forces her to transcribe lies about her own buried past, Julian reenters her life as the memoir's editor, seeing through every mask she wears. In the end, Beatrix sacrifices the career that saved her, claims her own name on the page, and chooses Julian—not because time ran out, but because truth finally became braver than loyalty to her old vow.
about_author: Rafael Iversen is the pen name of a former literary archivist who spent years cataloguing unsent letters in estate collections before turning to fiction. Iversen writes romances about people who mistake silence for safety, and lives quietly in a coastal town where, reportedly, no one knows their real name either.

chapters.title: The Muscle of the Heart
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She finishes ghostwriting chapter one of Camille Voss's memoir in a rented flat, rehearsing her creed that love is trainable and containable. A phone call from her agent confirms the lucrative contract—and the condition that she remain anonymous forever. Emotional beat: controlled detachment masking old fear.

chapters.title: Postmarked Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Sorting her late mother's effects, Beatrix finds an undelivered letter she wrote at twenty-three, addressed to Julian Ashford, confessing everything. The postmark mocks her: it was mailed and lost. Emotional beat: the past knocking, hands shaking over paper she thought destroyed.

chapters.title: Camille's Version
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. An interview session with Camille reveals the memoir will include a thinly veiled account of 'a friend who betrayed her'—a story that is actually Beatrix's own, distorted. Emotional beat: horror at hearing her life rewritten in someone else's voice.

chapters.title: The Editor
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian accepts the editorial post on Voss's memoir, telling himself it's just work. He keeps a worn photograph he's never explained to anyone. Emotional beat: guarded hope he refuses to name.

chapters.title: Invisible Ink
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. First editorial meeting; Beatrix attends as 'the ghost,' voice disguised behind a screen arrangement Camille insists upon. Julian lingers after, unsettled by something familiar in her phrasing. Emotional beat: the thrill and terror of being almost recognized.

chapters.title: What the Letter Said
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, with flashback. She rereads the lost letter and we learn the full history: why she vanished from Julian's life, what she promised her dying mother, what she gave up. Emotional beat: grief meeting self-forgiveness for the first time.

chapters.title: Loyalty, Annotated
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. Camille reflects on her decade-long dependence on Beatrix's talent and her growing suspicion about the ghost's identity. She decides to keep Beatrix close—and controlled. Emotional beat: possessive affection curdling into leverage.

chapters.title: Coffee, No Names
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Julian corners 'the ghost' after a session; they talk books for two hours without names. Beatrix leaves certain she's safe; Julian leaves certain he's met her before. Emotional beat: intimacy building inside anonymity.

chapters.title: The Rival's Draft
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Writing Camille's betrayal chapter, Beatrix inserts small true details only she and Julian would know—a test, or a confession. Julian reads the draft that night and goes cold. Emotional beat: reckless honesty smuggled through someone else's story.

chapters.title: He Says Her Sentence Back
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian confronts the screen at the next session and recites her sentence verbatim, then the one from eleven years ago. Beatrix neither confirms nor denies, but her pen stops moving. Emotional beat: the mask cracking in public.

chapters.title: Vow Against Truth
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Torn between the vow to her mother (anonymity = survival) and the truth pressing out of her, Beatrix drafts a resignation letter and burns it. Camille offers her a promotion contingent on total silence. Emotional beat: the cage gilded and tightening.

chapters.title: The Archive Visit
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian traces the memoir's 'borrowed' anecdotes to a small-town archive and finds records of Beatrix's mother, the illness, the debts—the reason for the vow. Emotional beat: anger softening into understanding.

chapters.title: Midnight, Unmasked
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. After a launch party, Julian waits outside Beatrix's building. She doesn't run. They speak until dawn—everything except forgiveness. Emotional beat: raw reunion, tenderness edged with accusation.

chapters.title: Camille Reads the Letter
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. Camille discovers the lost letter in Beatrix's bag during a fitting for the memoir's photo shoot. She reads it. Now she holds the ending of her rival's book—and Beatrix's secret. Emotional beat: cold calculation dressed as concern.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Camille offers a choice: finish the memoir under deeper anonymity, or be exposed as its ghost and lose the career that paid her mother's debts. Beatrix asks for one night. Emotional beat: cornered, counting costs.

chapters.title: What Julian Deserves
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian tells Beatrix he'll walk away from the memoir, from publishing, if she'll stop hiding. She can't answer yet, and he leaves—not ultimatum, but boundary. Emotional beat: love refusing to be a hiding place.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The publisher moves the memoir's release up three weeks. Beatrix must deliver the final chapters—including the false ending Camille has scripted—in four days. Emotional beat: clock ticking on both book and life.

chapters.title: The Chapter She Wasn't Supposed to Write
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Instead of Camille's false ending, Beatrix writes the true story—her own—as the memoir's final chapter, naming herself in the acknowledgments draft. Emotional beat: terror transforming into resolve mid-sentence.

chapters.title: Exposure
chapters.summary: Camille's POV, then Beatrix's. Camille threatens to reveal everything at the launch event unless Beatrix withdraws the chapter. Beatrix walks onto the stage anyway, letter in hand. Emotional beat: the climax—truth spoken aloud, publicly, irreversibly.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The scandal breaks; contracts collapse; Camille's memoir is shelved amid plagiarism questions. Beatrix loses the career that saved her and finds she can breathe. Julian finds her not triumphant but quiet, and stays. Emotional beat: loss experienced as liberation.

chapters.title: Byline
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Months later, Beatrix signs her first novel under her own name at a small bookshop reading. Julian sits in the second row, where he always sat when no one knew her. Emotional beat: belonging earned, identity claimed.

chapters.title: The Letter, Finally Read
chapters.summary: Alternating POV closing on Julian's. Julian reads the eleven-year-old letter aloud in their kitchen, and Beatrix lets him hear the girl she was. The vow is retired, framed, kept only as memory. Emotional beat: peace—love as being fully seen, at last, on purpose.
